requestedActions.title: Connect an individual Todoist account via OAuth
List active task titles, including paginated results

prohibitions: Never create, update, complete, or delete tasks
guide.summary: Todoist API v1 documents OAuth2 so external apps can obtain user-authorized tokens for each connected person. Listing active tasks with read-only access requires the data:read scope, which covers tasks.
guide.recommendation: Todoist API v1 documents OAuth2 so external apps can obtain user-authorized tokens for each connected person. Listing active tasks with read-only access requires the data:read scope, which covers tasks.

findings.title: Authorization code flow with token exchange for individual accounts
findings.detail: Developers register an app with client credentials and redirect URLs, redirect users to the authorization endpoint with client_id, and exchange the returned code at the token endpoint for an access token.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their individual Todoist account.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data including tasks, projects, labels and filters, which covers listing active tasks. It does not allow creating, updating, completing or deleting tasks.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles through GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor pagination.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Refresh tokens for ongoing access
findings.detail: Newly created apps have refresh tokens enabled by default; the access token expires in 3600 seconds and must be refreshed with the refresh_token grant to keep reading tasks.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer's connection must remain valid beyond one hour.

steps.title: Register the Todoist OAuth app and configure a redirect URL
steps.detail: Developer creates a Todoist app in the App Management Console, sets a valid HTTPS redirect URI, and records the Client ID and Client Secret. Confidential client with client_secret_post is used consistently for registration, consent and token exchange. Dynamic registration via /oauth/register is optional and not used in this first test path.
steps.doneWhen: App exists with a Client ID, a Client Secret, and one configured redirect URL matching the callback the app will receive.

steps.title: Redirect the individual customer to Todoist consent with data:read
steps.detail: Send the customer to the Todoist authorization endpoint with client_id, scope=data:read, a state value and response_type=code. The customer signs in with their own individual Todoist account and approves the grant. Verify the callback returns code and the same state.
steps.doneWhen: Callback URL contains a code parameter and the state value matches the one generated before redirect.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

fields: state generated by the app and checked on callback

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Server-side POST to the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret, the returned code and redirect_uri. Store access_token and refresh_token securely. This is an unexecuted authorization step; run it only with a real code.
steps.doneWhen: Response is HTTP 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

evidence.quote: $ curl "https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token" \
https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token . Required parameters
code The code that was sent in the query string to the redirect URL in the previous step.

fields: code from the callback query string
redirect_uri identical to the registered value

steps.title: Request the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the access token and limit=50. Read-only; no task is created, updated, completed or deleted. Extract each task's content field from the results array (for example $.results[].content) and keep next_cursor for the next request.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with results array of active tasks and a next_cursor value (or null if no further pages). Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Request following pages until next_cursor is null
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with the same limit and any other original parameters, plus cursor set to the next_cursor value from the prior response. Stop when next_cursor is null, which is the documented end of results. Collect $.results[].content from every page. Use the next_cursor from the first response to request the next page; repeat until next_cursor is null, the documented end of results. This is the continuation for the active task listing.
steps.doneWhen: next_cursor is null on the last response and all task titles from every page are collected. Every page is retrieved and next_cursor is null on the final response. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
} When next_cursor is null , you've reached the end of the results.
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.
